sentences.zh: 你知道，就像我们家一样，回家后你得做家务，有各种事情要做。

sentences.en: But I do feel like being born a girl in an Arab household did have these kind of cultural expectations of me that, you know, no boyfriends.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得，作为一个出生在阿拉伯家庭的女孩，我背负着某种文化期望，比如，你知道的，不能交男朋友。

sentences.en: Um, it's just girls don't curse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是女孩不能说脏话。

sentences.en: I started cursing very young.
sentences.zh: 我从很小的时候就开始说脏话了。

sentences.en: Most teenagers find a way to rebel.
sentences.zh: 大多数青少年都会找到反叛的方式。

sentences.en: And knowing what I know about you, I have to imagine that you are rebellious.
sentences.zh: 而且据我对你的了解，我不得不认为你是个叛逆的人。

sentences.en: When did you start to become someone who was rebelling against your parents and your family?
sentences.zh: 你是从什么时候开始变成一个反抗父母和家庭的人的？

sentences.en: Probably when I was 15.
sentences.zh: 大概是15岁的时候吧。

sentences.zh: 那时发生了什么？

sentences.zh: “不行”，就是指不能参加某些旅行，或者不能参与学校里的某些活动。

sentences.en: And this, you know, this is to protect you, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这都是为了保护你，明白吗？

sentences.en: And, uh, so I pushed up against that.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我就对此进行了反抗。

sentences.en: I mean, it was huge fights, explosive fights.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那都是些激烈的争吵，爆发性的争吵。

sentences.en: When you're having conflicts with your parents at this age, so maybe middle school, high school, what, what are those conflicts?
sentences.zh: 当你在这个年纪，比如初中、高中时与父母发生冲突，那些冲突具体是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, like the senior trip, prom, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，比如毕业旅行、舞会之类的。

sentences.en: It's like, what's that?
sentences.zh: 就像是，那是什么？

sentences.en: It was, it, those are the difficulties of, you know, being a child of immigrants and them truly not
sentences.zh: 那是，那是作为移民子女的困难，他们真的不

sentences.en: understanding like, you know, this is, and did I really truly needed all those things?
sentences.zh: 理解，你知道，这是，我真的需要所有那些东西吗？

sentences.en: I don't know, but I didn't want to be left out of all the celebrations and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，但我不想被排除在所有的庆祝活动之外。

sentences.en: So I got to go to prom, but I had to take my brother.
sentences.zh: 所以我得以去参加舞会，但我必须带上我哥哥。

sentences.en: You couldn't take a date?
sentences.zh: 你不能带舞伴吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: Because a date you represent what?
sentences.zh: 因为带舞伴意味着什么？

sentences.en: No, we couldn't have boyfriends.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不能交男朋友。

sentences.en: You couldn't have a boyfriend?
sentences.zh: 你不能交男朋友？

sentences.en: You're a senior in high school.
sentences.zh: 你可是高中生了。

sentences.en: Oh no, there's no boyfriends?
sentences.zh: 哦不，完全不能交男朋友？

sentences.en: Are you serious?
sentences.zh: 你是认真的吗？

sentences.zh: 我21岁就结婚了。

sentences.en: One.
sentences.zh: 一。

sentences.en: Because at one point, the nose just got so frustrating and got to the point where, I mean, as I got older, more womanly, I guess, I don't know, that my dad and my mom were like,
sentences.zh: 因为有段时间，那些“不行”实在太让人沮丧了，到了那种地步，我是说，随着我长大，变得更有女人味，我猜，我不知道，我爸妈就觉得，

sentences.en: it was lockdown.
sentences.zh: 那是封锁状态。

sentences.en: It was school and home and it wasn't, you know, I wanted to go on trips.
sentences.zh: 就是学校和家，没有别的，你知道，我想去旅行。

sentences.en: I wanted to possibly study abroad and all that wasn't going to be possible.
sentences.zh: 我可能想出国留学，但这一切都不可能实现。

sentences.en: And then I, I remember meeting this guy, my future husband, super quiet, shy, super sweet.
sentences.zh: 然后我，我记得遇到了这个男人，我未来的丈夫，超级安静，害羞，超级贴心。

sentences.en: And I joke, when he said, I was like, I, I got married.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑说，当他说的时候，我就像，我，我结婚了。

sentences.en: I needed to get, and he goes, you're using me.
sentences.zh: 我需要得到，他说，你在利用我。

sentences.en: And it's like, we were very much in love.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们确实非常相爱。

sentences.en: Um, but you can't yada, yada, yada your way through marriage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你不能靠敷衍了事来维持婚姻。

sentences.en: So my question is, it was a kind of escape from a certain kind of childhood.
sentences.zh: 所以我的问题是，这算是一种逃离某种童年的方式吗？

sentences.en: And my husband at that time, we were, I mean, fiance, he wanted to stay engaged longer.
sentences.zh: 当时我的丈夫，我们，我是说，未婚夫，他想延长订婚时间。

sentences.en: And I was the one like, no, we need to get married.
sentences.zh: 而我是那个说，不，我们需要结婚的人。

sentences.en: Like you could leave the house.
sentences.zh: 就像你可以离开家一样。

sentences.en: I could leave, but I also told him even dating would be a problem.
sentences.zh: 我可以离开，但我还告诉他，即使是约会也会是个问题。

sentences.en: You know, any of that would have been like this constant struggle with them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何那种事都会变成和他们不断的斗争。

sentences.en: It was overly protective.
sentences.zh: 这太过度保护了。

sentences.en: I think they didn't know any way of being parents.
sentences.zh: 我想他们不知道还有什么别的做父母的方式。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的，这一个月你可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: How much a part of your childhood was your Muslim identity?
sentences.zh: 你的穆斯林身份在你的童年中占了多大比重？

sentences.en: How big a part of your life was that?
sentences.zh: 那在你生活中占了多大分量？

sentences.en: I mean, I grew up more Palestinian than Muslim or even Arab.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我成长过程中更多是作为巴勒斯坦人，而不是穆斯林，甚至不是阿拉伯人。

sentences.en: I mean, I think being Palestinian, especially in the 80s and 90s and everything that was happening,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为作为巴勒斯坦人，尤其是在80年代和90年代，以及当时发生的一切，

sentences.en: it's like constantly in the news, it was constantly, you know, topic of conversation at gatherings.
sentences.zh: 就像不断出现在新闻里，不断地，你知道，成为聚会上的谈资。

sentences.en: Um, you know, people, we would be in settings where I'm like, they're like, oh, I'm 1948.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，人们，我们会在一些场合，我听到他们说，哦，我是1948年的。

sentences.en: Like in 1948, he was displaced and he had to leave.
sentences.zh: 就像在1948年，他流离失所，不得不离开。

sentences.en: With the creation of Israel.
sentences.zh: 随着以色列的建立。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or I'm, oh, I'm 67, you know, so displaced in 1967.
sentences.zh: 或者我是，哦，我是67年的，你知道，所以在1967年流离失所。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so all of that was so, you know, as a young child, like you can hear like, and these are people that you're interacting with at weddings and gatherings and things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些，你知道，作为一个小孩，你会听到，而这些人都是你在婚礼和聚会上互动的人。

sentences.en: And so with that in mind, what's the story that you are absorbing about the Palestinian-Israeli conflict?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到这一点，你所吸收的关于巴以冲突的故事是什么？

sentences.en: You're hearing bits and pieces of it, but by the time you're in high school, what's the story that you, as you understand it, of the conflict?
sentences.zh: 你听到了一些零碎的信息，但当你上高中时，你所理解的这场冲突的故事是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, so I went to a predominantly black high school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，我上的是一所黑人占多数的高中。

sentences.en: And it was the first year that Detroit Public Schools started, um, requiring African-American history.
sentences.zh: 那是底特律公立学校开始，嗯，要求教授非裔美国人历史的第一年。

sentences.en: And I remember we got these, I want to say they were orange, brand new books.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们拿到了这些，我想应该是橙色的，全新的书。

sentences.en: And they were all talking about segregation, some of the most oppressive times of black Americans in our country, all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 书里都在谈论种族隔离，谈论美国黑人历史上一些最压抑的时期，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And as they were talking, there were so many similarities of what I saw as a 12-year-old with my mom.
sentences.zh: 当他们谈论这些时，我发现这和我12岁时跟我妈看到的有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: Um, I remember we were going for my uncle's wedding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得我们当时要去参加我叔叔的婚礼。

sentences.en: In the Palestinian territories?
sentences.zh: 在巴勒斯坦领土上？

sentences.en: In the Palestinian territories.
sentences.zh: 在巴勒斯坦领土上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Even at the airport, how we were treated there to, you know, segregated lines to even when we were trying to go to my grandfather's house,
sentences.zh: 即使在机场，我们受到的对待，你知道，隔离的排队，甚至当我们试图去我祖父家时，

sentences.en: we had to go through maybe, I don't know what you want to call Israel or Palestine.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不穿过，我不知道你该称之为以色列还是巴勒斯坦。

sentences.en: I don't know how, where it was at that moment.
sentences.zh: 我不知道当时那是哪里。

sentences.en: I was 12.
sentences.zh: 我当时12岁。

sentences.en: But I know we had to go through a checkpoint.
sentences.zh: 但我知道我们必须通过一个检查站。

sentences.en: There was two different color license plates, yellow and blue.
sentences.zh: 有两种不同颜色的车牌，黄色和蓝色。

sentences.en: So if you had blue license plates, you couldn't, like, travel in certain areas or something.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有蓝色车牌，你就不能在某些地区行驶之类的。

sentences.en: So it was very segregated.
sentences.zh: 所以那是相当隔离的。

sentences.en: And then, for me, that connectivity of what African-American struggle went through with segregation and oppression and equality.
sentences.zh: 然后，对我来说，非裔美国人经历的种族隔离、压迫和平等斗争，这种联系感。

sentences.en: Like, the fact that you're born here, but you're not equal because of the color of your skin.
sentences.zh: 就像，你出生在这里，但因为肤色而不平等的事实。

sentences.en: And so thinking about my grandmother, who was born there, but doesn't have equality, is treated less than.
sentences.zh: 所以想到我的祖母，她出生在那里，却没有平等，被视为低人一等。

sentences.en: As a Palestinian.
sentences.zh: 作为巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: As a Palestinian.
sentences.zh: 作为巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So much of that is connected.
sentences.zh: 其中很多都是相连的。

sentences.en: To growing up in the city of Detroit, to seeing what's happening to my ancestors in Palestine, there's so much connectivity.
sentences.zh: 在底特律长大，看到我的祖先在巴勒斯坦发生的事情，这种联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: And that's how I see it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我看待它的方式。

sentences.en: What was the basic story that your mom and dad, having come from the Palestinian territories, that they told you about what had happened?
sentences.zh: 你父母从巴勒斯坦领土来到这里，他们告诉你的关于所发生之事的原始故事是什么？

sentences.en: Growing up, my dad, for him, it's like our land was taken.
sentences.zh: 成长过程中，对我父亲来说，就像我们的土地被夺走了。

sentences.en: We were uprooted.
sentences.zh: 我们被连根拔起。

sentences.en: It was about power and about struggle.
sentences.zh: 那是关于权力和斗争。

sentences.en: And then I started seeking it out myself.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始自己去探寻。

sentences.en: I think even starting with what happened in the Holocaust and how that led to the movement of creating a Jewish state, right?
sentences.zh: 我想甚至从大屠杀中发生的事情，以及它是如何导致建立犹太国家运动的开始，对吧？

sentences.en: All that part wasn't really explained, right?
sentences.zh: 所有那部分并没有真正被解释清楚，对吧？

sentences.en: This sense of safe haven.
sentences.zh: 这种避风港的感觉。

sentences.en: It almost gave you a little bit of peace of like, okay, all right, I get it, all right.
sentences.zh: 它几乎给了你一点平静，就像，好吧，好的，我明白了，好的。

sentences.en: But then how do you equate that as like, was it really truly okay then to completely displace a whole people?
sentences.zh: 但你如何将其等同于，那么彻底地流离失所整个民族真的是对的吗？

sentences.en: To take away everything that they know, their way of life, their land, all of that.
sentences.zh: 夺走他们所知道的一切，他们的生活方式，他们的土地，所有这些。

sentences.en: You were in law school when 9-11 happened.
sentences.zh: 9-11发生时你正在读法学院。

sentences.en: And can you tell me about that?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我关于那件事吗？

sentences.en: I was taking weekend classes.
sentences.zh: 我当时在上周末课程。

sentences.en: I can't remember what, and it was during the week that it happened.
sentences.zh: 我不记得是什么了，那是发生在工作日。

sentences.en: It was a weekday.
sentences.zh: 那是工作日。

sentences.en: Because I worked full-time.
sentences.zh: 因为我全职工作。

sentences.en: I was the executive assistant to the largest Arab American Human Services Agency in the country, Access.
sentences.zh: 我是全国最大的阿拉伯裔美国人公共服务机构Access的行政助理。

sentences.en: And that morning, it was like maybe between 8 or 9 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 那天早上，大概在早上8点到9点之间。

sentences.en: People were in the lunchroom, very small, very, very small room.
sentences.zh: 人们在午餐室里，非常小，非常非常小的房间。

sentences.en: I didn't know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: But then I heard gasps, and then I ran, and I saw a couple of my colleagues crying.
sentences.zh: 但后来我听到惊呼声，然后我跑过去，看到几个同事在哭。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, my God, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，发生了什么？

sentences.en: We started seeing these images, and then we can hear like the screams from the TV.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到这些画面，然后我们可以听到电视里传来的尖叫声。

sentences.en: We all started crying, and I was like, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 我们都开始哭，我当时想，天哪。

sentences.en: And then not even within like an hour or two, we had to stop mourning because we started getting calls of threatening calls.
sentences.zh: 然后甚至不到一两个小时，我们就不得不停止哀悼，因为我们开始接到威胁电话。

sentences.en: Our executive director was driving in, and some young people showed up and started throwing bottles.
sentences.zh: 我们的执行董事开车进来时，一些年轻人出现并开始扔瓶子。

sentences.en: At that moment, it became very real that being Muslim in America was going to be completely different.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，成为美国的穆斯林将变得完全不同，这一点变得非常真实。

sentences.en: My sister, who was in, I think, third grade, Layla, came home upset and saying that somebody in her class,
sentences.zh: 我妹妹，我想她在读三年级，莱拉，回家时很难过，说她班上有个人，

sentences.en: because the teacher asked if anybody had any questions, and somebody in her class raised her hand and said, does this mean we have to kill Layla?
sentences.zh: 因为老师问有没有人有问题，她班上有个人举手说，这是否意味着我们必须杀了莱拉？

sentences.en: And then my other brother, somebody called the 800 number on him, and sure enough, the FBI showed up at his home.
sentences.zh: 然后我另一个哥哥，有人拨打了针对他的800热线，果然，联邦调查局出现在他家门口。

sentences.en: People probably don't remember, but after 9-11, they kept putting this 800 number up and say, call if you have any suspicious person.
sentences.zh: 人们可能不记得了，但在9-11之后，他们一直发布这个800热线，说如果你有可疑人员就打电话。

sentences.en: So they called on him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们举报了他。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, you got to meet with Rashad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你得去见见拉沙德。

sentences.en: Like, he's not, he's just a, he was kind of a punk kid back then, and just like partied like everybody else, and always worried that he wasn't going to class.
sentences.zh: 他不是，他只是个，他当时是个小混混，就像其他人一样参加派对，总是担心自己没去上课。

sentences.en: I constantly called him.
sentences.zh: 我不断地给他打电话。

sentences.en: And then my parents were interviewed by the FBI.
sentences.zh: 然后我父母接受了联邦调查局的采访。

sentences.en: It was horrifying because when they showed up to my mom's house, they surrounded the house.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了，因为当他们出现在我妈妈家时，他们包围了房子。

sentences.en: Like, it was a military operation with, you know, big guns and everything.
sentences.zh: 就像是一场军事行动，你知道，带着大枪什么的。

sentences.en: My sister was so little, and she's like, mama, what's all that?
sentences.zh: 我妹妹还那么小，她说，妈妈，那是什么？

sentences.en: And they're all around the house, and came barging in.
sentences.zh: 他们围着房子，然后闯了进来。

sentences.en: It scared the shit out of my mom.
sentences.zh: 这把我妈吓坏了。

sentences.en: They spent the most time with my father.
sentences.zh: 他们花在跟我父亲谈话上的时间最多。

sentences.en: They went from the first time my dad came to the country and went through every single thing.
sentences.zh: 他们从我父亲第一次来到这个国家开始，把每一件事都过了一遍。

sentences.en: They already knew all the answers.
sentences.zh: 他们已经知道所有答案了。

sentences.en: And my dad stayed calm.
sentences.zh: 但我父亲保持冷静。

sentences.en: And didn't, you know, he looked tired after it was done.
sentences.zh: 而且没有，你知道，结束后他看起来很累。

sentences.en: My mother was confused constantly.
sentences.zh: 我母亲一直很困惑。

sentences.en: They kept showing her pictures, whether you know this person or the other.
sentences.zh: 他们不停地给她看照片，问你认不认识这个人或那个人。

sentences.en: She goes, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不认识。

sentences.en: They all look alike.

sentences.zh: 但我感到有更大的责任去发声。

sentences.en: The more they try to shut me up, the more I speak out.
sentences.zh: 他们越是想让我闭嘴，我就越要发声。

sentences.en: The more they try to bully me, the more I speak out, you know that even on BDS, I never had a stance on it until they tried to criminalize it, you know?
sentences.zh: 他们越是想霸凌我，我就越要发声。你知道，即使是在BDS（抵制、撤资、制裁运动）问题上，在他们试图将其定罪之前，我从未有过立场，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So when your colleague said that boycotting and divesting from Israel should be much harder to do, that's when you decided, I'm going to support this.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你的同事说抵制以色列和从以色列撤资应该变得更难时，你才决定支持这一立场。

sentences.en: I actually came out when I heard they're going to move the anti-BDS bill, and the first thing I thought about was all the young people, everybody that I've met that truly believes
sentences.zh: 其实，当我听说他们要推动反BDS法案时，我站了出来。我首先想到的是所有年轻人，我见过的每一个真正相信

sentences.en: in economic boycott, but also growing up here, we learned about how economic boycott got us closer to at least a viable civil rights movement in our country.
sentences.zh: 经济抵制的人。而且，在这里长大的过程中，我们了解到经济抵制是如何让我们国家至少更接近一场可行的民权运动的。

sentences.en: Do you see all of this as kind of the inevitability of diversity in Congress?
sentences.zh: 你是否认为这一切都是国会多元化带来的必然结果？

sentences.en: Is it inevitable that with a more diverse group of lawmakers in the House will come perspectives that are going to challenge the way that the party approaches this?
sentences.zh: 随着众议院议员群体变得更加多元，是否必然会出现挑战党派处理此类问题方式的观点？

sentences.en: The party line on Israel, having the daughter, the granddaughter of a Palestinian living in the West Banking, the party in the House.
sentences.zh: 关于以色列的党派路线，考虑到有一位住在西岸的巴勒斯坦人的女儿、孙女在众议院，党派路线……

sentences.en: I don't even just think it's this issue.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这仅仅是这一个问题。

sentences.en: I think it's a lot of other issues, issues around poverty, issues around LGBTQ, issues around immigration, all of those issues that we're facing, economic justice.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有很多其他问题，比如贫困问题、LGBTQ问题、移民问题，以及我们面临的所有这些问题，还有经济正义。

sentences.en: This class is bolder, more courageous, and it's not just the four that everybody concentrates on.
sentences.zh: 这一届议员更大胆、更勇敢，而且不仅仅是大家关注的那四个人。

sentences.en: It is an incredible class.
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的群体。

sentences.en: Some of the people that picked up seats that were previously held by Republicans sign on to the Green New Deal.
sentences.zh: 一些从共和党手中夺回席位的议员签署了“绿色新政”。

sentences.en: Some are on supporting Medicare for all.
sentences.zh: 有些人支持“全民医保”。

sentences.en: You wouldn't have saw that a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 几年前你可看不到这些。

sentences.en: So I say this a lot, but yeah, we look differently, but we also serve and fight differently, this new Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常说，是的，我们看起来不同，但我们这一届新国会服务和战斗的方式也不同。

sentences.en: Actually, does it feel different, our visit now, than before?
sentences.zh: 说真的，我们现在的这次访问，感觉和以前有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: And if so, what about it feels different?
sentences.zh: 如果有，哪里让你觉得不同？

sentences.en: When you first met me, I just, this was, you know, I just felt like there was this big rainbow outside.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次见到我时，我只是……你知道，我当时觉得外面有一道巨大的彩虹。

sentences.en: It was just like looming over the Capitol, but then the storms came, the lightning, all of that came, and it's much more of a difficult journey.
sentences.zh: 它就像笼罩在国会大厦上空，但随后风暴来了，闪电来了，所有这些都来了，这段旅程变得艰难得多。

sentences.en: And I still feel it, but it's, it feels different.
sentences.zh: 我依然有这种感觉，但它……感觉确实不同了。

sentences.en: It's much harder than I thought, that you want to change the world, that it's all before me.
sentences.zh: 这比我想象的要难得多，你想改变世界，而一切都在我面前。

sentences.en: And it's tough.
sentences.zh: 这很艰难。

sentences.en: It's tougher than people think.

sentences.en: Over the weekend, in an interview on the Yahoo podcast, Skullduggery, Rashida Tlaib was asked
sentences.zh: 周末，在雅虎播客《Skullduggery》的采访中，拉希达·特莱布被问及

sentences.en: about her position, that the solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict would be to create a single state for Israelis and Palestinians, rather than two separate states.
sentences.zh: 她的立场，即解决巴以冲突的方案应该是为以色列人和巴勒斯坦人建立一个单一国家，而不是两个独立的国家。

sentences.en: So what is your vision for a one-state solution that meets both Palestinian and Israeli Jewish national aspirations?
sentences.zh: 那么，你对一个既能满足巴勒斯坦人又能满足以色列犹太民族愿望的“一国方案”有何愿景？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And let me tell you, I mean, for me,
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你，我的意思是，对我来说，

sentences.en: just a few, I think two weeks ago or so, we celebrated or just, it took a moment, I think, in our country to remember the Holocaust.
sentences.zh: 就在几周前，我想大概两周前，我们庆祝了，或者说，我认为我们国家花了一点时间来纪念大屠杀。

sentences.en: And there's, you know, there's a kind of a calming feeling I always tell folks when I think of
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我想到

sentences.en: the Holocaust and the tragedy of the Holocaust and the fact that it was my ancestors, Palestinians
sentences.zh: 大屠杀以及大屠杀的悲剧时，我总是告诉人们有一种平静的感觉。事实上，正是我的祖先——巴勒斯坦人，

sentences.en: who lost their land and some lost their lives, their livelihood, the human dignity, their existence in many ways have been wiped out on some people's passport.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了土地，有些人失去了生命、生计，人类尊严，他们的存在在很多方面都被某些人的护照抹去了。

sentences.en: I mean, just all of it, was in the name of trying to create a safe haven for Jews post the Holocaust,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这一切，都是以在大屠杀后为犹太人创造一个安全避风港的名义进行的，

sentences.en: post the tragedy and horrific persecution of Jews across the world at that time.
sentences.zh: 在大屠杀之后，在当时世界各地犹太人遭受悲剧和可怕迫害之后。

sentences.en: Many House Republicans have responded by suggesting Tlaib meant that the Holocaust itself gave her
sentences.zh: 许多众议院共和党人回应称，特莱布的意思是大屠杀本身给了她

sentences.en: a calming feeling, not the creation of a state for the Jewish people following the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 一种平静的感觉，而不是大屠杀后为犹太人民建立一个国家。

sentences.en: And I love the fact that it was my ancestors that provided that, right, in many ways, but they did it in a way that took their human dignity away, right?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样一个事实，即正是我的祖先提供了这一点，对吧，在很多方面，但他们这样做的方式剥夺了他们的人类尊严，对吧？

sentences.en: And it was forced on them.
sentences.zh: 而且这是强加给他们的。

sentences.en: And so when I think about one state, I think about the fact that why couldn't we do it in a better way?
sentences.zh: 所以当我想到“一国方案”时，我想到的是，为什么我们不能用更好的方式来做呢？

sentences.en: Others have criticized Tlaib for misrepresenting history in seeming to suggest that the Palestinians
sentences.zh: 其他人批评特莱布歪曲历史，似乎暗示巴勒斯坦人

sentences.en: played a role in the creation of a safe haven for Jews, rather than opposing it.
sentences.zh: 在为犹太人创造安全避风港的过程中发挥了作用，而不是反对它。

sentences.en: On Sunday night, Tlaib defended herself, tweeting, quote,
sentences.zh: 周日晚上，特莱布为自己辩护，发推文称，引用：

sentences.en: Policing my words, twisting and turning them to ignite vile attacks on me, will not work.
sentences.zh: 监管我的言论，扭曲和歪曲它们来煽动对我的恶毒攻击，是不会得逞的。

sentences.en: All of you who are trying to silence me will fail miserably.
sentences.zh: 你们所有试图让我噤声的人都将惨败。

sentences.en: I will never allow you to take my words out of context, to push your racist and hateful agenda.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会允许你们断章取义，来推行你们种族主义和仇恨的议程。

sentences.en: The truth will always win.
sentences.zh: 真相终将获胜。

sentences.zh: 周一，特朗普总统在推特上发表评论称，特莱布“显然对以色列和犹太人民怀有巨大的仇恨”。
